html:
Erik the Red was a Norse settler who founded the first European colony in Greenland around 985. Born in Norway, he moved to Iceland with his father, who had been exiled for killings.

Outlawed from Iceland for three years after more killings, Erik sailed west and explored the coast of Greenland. The sagas say he named it Greenland so that people would want to go there.

He returned with about 25 ships of settlers, of which 14 arrived, and built his farm at Brattahlid in the south. His son Leif Erikson sailed on to Vinland in North America. The Norse settlements he founded lasted about 450 years. The story is told in the Icelandic sagas.
